title: How many WSOP bracelets will the 2026 Main Event winner hold at the end of the 2026 WSOP season?
short_title: 2026 WSOP Main Event winner total bracelets?
description:
The World Series of Poker (WSOP) is the most prestigious poker tournament series in the world, awarding [gold bracelets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Series_of_Poker_bracelet) to event winners. The [2026 WSOP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Series_of_Poker) is the 57th edition of the series, running from May 26 through July 15 in Las Vegas, with 100 gold bracelets to be awarded. The centerpiece is the \$10,000 No-Limit Hold'em Main Event, regularly attracting around ten thousand entrants, from amateur qualifiers to seasoned professionals. The Main Event begins July 2, with play continuing until the final table is reached on July 13. The final table will then take place from August 3–5, airing live on ESPN.

A list of previous WSOP Main Event winners along with their total bracelet counts can be found on [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_of_Poker_Main_Event_champions).
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the total number of WSOP bracelets held by the winner of the 2026 World Series of Poker Main Event at the conclusion of the 2026 WSOP season, per [official WSOP records](https://www.wsop.com/past-tournaments/2026/).
fine_print:
The question will resolve as the total number of bracelets won by the winner, not the number of bracelets won in 2026. The 2026 WSOP Main Event bracelet will itself count towards the total.

If the 2026 WSOP Main Event is cancelled or otherwise a winner cannot be determined by September 1, 2026, this question will be annulled.

title: Will WHO declare hantavirus a Public Health Emergency of International Concern before 2027?
short_title: Hantavirus PHEIC before 2027?
description:
[Hantavirus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hantavirus_infection) is the disease caused by the Orthohantavirus genus of viruses carried by rodents. Human infections usually occur through contact with aerosolized urine, droppings, or saliva from infected rodents, though rare person-to-person transmission has been documented for the [Andes virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andes_virus), a hantavirus found in parts of South America. Hantavirus infection can cause severe disease, including hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, which can progress rapidly and has a high fatality rate.

In May 2026, WHO [reported](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON599) a cluster of hantavirus cases linked to the [MV *Hondius*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Hondius) cruise ship. As of WHO's 7 May update, eight cases had been reported, including three deaths, and five cases had been laboratory-confirmed. WHO stated that it was supporting affected countries with surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention guidance, and medical evacuation coordination.

A [Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_health_emergency_of_international_concern) is WHO’s highest formal alert under the International Health Regulations. It refers to an extraordinary event that poses a public health risk to other countries through international spread and may require a coordinated international response. Past PHEICs have been declared for events such as H1N1 influenza, polio, Ebola, Zika, COVID-19, and mpox.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, prior to January 1, 2027, a hantavirus or an outbreak caused by a hantavirus is declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) by the World Health Organization.
fine_print:
* The PHEIC must be declared as a result of a human outbreak, not in response to an animal outbreak of the virus or the effects of the virus spreading in non-human species (i.e. shortages of food).
* For this question to resolve **Yes**, the declaration must explicitly identify hantavirus, a named hantavirus such as Andes virus, or a hantavirus-linked outbreak as the disease/event underlying the PHEIC. A PHEIC declaration that includes hantavirus only as a secondary or incidental concern will not count unless hantavirus is a central cause of the declared emergency.

title: Who will be Iran's Supreme Leader on January 1, 2027?
short_title: Who will be Iran's Supreme Leader on Jan 1, 2027?
description:
On 28 February 2026, [Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Khamenei) was killed during a series of airstrikes conducted by Israel and the United States. Khamenei had not officially declared a successor prior to his death, though the [New York Times reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/21/world/middleeast/iran-ayatollah-israel-war.html) that he had privately nominated three senior clerics as potential successors: [Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gholam-Hossein_Mohseni-Eje%27i), [Asghar Hijazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asghar_Hijazi), and [Hassan Khomeini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hassan_Khomeini).

Under Article 111 of Iran's constitution, a temporary three-member council [was formed](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/1/who-could-succeed-ayatollah-ali-khamenei-to-lead-iran) to handle executive duties until a new Supreme Leader is selected. That council consists of President Masoud Pezeshkian, Supreme Court Chief Justice Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i, and senior cleric Ayatollah Alireza Arafi, who was appointed from the Guardian Council. Iran's Supreme Leader is formally chosen by the Assembly of Experts, an 88-member clerical body, by simple majority vote. Among [the most frequently discussed candidates](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/succession-plans-irans-khamenei-hit-top-gear-2025-06-23/) is Hassan Khomeini, the 54-year-old grandson of the Islamic Republic's founder, who is considered a reformist figure. Other contenders include [Mojtaba Khamenei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojtaba_Khamenei), the late Supreme Leader's son, who has strong ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, though the clerical establishment may resist a father-to-son succession given the regime's revolutionary origins.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resove as the individual who is officially the Supreme Leader of Iran on January 1, 2027, at 00:00 Iran Standard Time.

If the position of Supreme Leader is formally abolished or the Islamic Republic of Iran ceases to exist, this question will resolve as **Position abolished**.

If no alive individual is the official Supreme Leader of Iran on January 1, 2027, this question will resolve as **None**.
fine_print:
Any interim, acting, or temporary leader will not count toward the resolution of this market.

Only individuals formally appointed to the office titled "Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran" (or a direct equivalent replacing that title) will qualify. Individuals serving solely as President, head of state, head of government, or in any other role that is not explicitly the Supreme Leader or a direct constitutional equivalent will not qualify.

title: When will a majority of G7 members recognize Palestinian statehood?
short_title: When will most G7 members recognize Palestine?
description:
Until July of 2025, no [G7 country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G7) had ever committed to recognizing Palestinian statehood. That changed when France [publicly committed](https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250724-french-president-macron-says-france-will-recognize-palestine-as-a-state-in-september) to recognizing Palestinian statehood at the upcoming UN General Assembly meeting in September. France's move comes as Palestine is under going a humanitarian catastrophe. Human rights groups say the Palestinian people are being subjected to a [genocide](https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/28/middleeast/israeli-human-rights-group-accuses-israel-genocide-gaza-intl) and [famine-like](https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/07/1165517) conditions due to Israeli occupation.

Less than a week after France's announcement, the UK [announced](https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cdrkj810plvt) they will do the same, but unlike France, it placed conditions on its recognition. The recognition of Palestine would not happen if Israel agreed to an imminent ceasefire, "flooded" Gaza with aid, among other measures.

As July 31st, Canada [also announced](https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/30/world/canada-recognize-palestinian-state-september-intl-latam) similar plans:

> 'Canada intends to recognize the state of Palestine at the 80th General Assembly of the United Nations,' Carney told reporters, flanked by Foreign Minister Anita Anand. 'We intend to do so because the Palestinian Authority has committed to lead much needed reform.'

Was France's recognition a tipping point for the West's approach to the Palestinian Question? Will it lead to a majority of G7 countries recognizing Palestinian statehood sometime before 2040?

Note that [147 of the 193 UN member states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_recognition_of_Palestine) already recognize Palestine.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the date when at least four of the G7 countries recognize Palestinian statehood.
fine_print:
* A country is considered is to have recognized Palestinian statehood when that country has said such in an official press release or document. Examples can be found [here](https://docs.un.org/en/A/78/846) and [here](https://www.gov.si/en/news/2024-06-05-republika-slovenija-in-drzava-palestina-vzpostavili-diplomatske-odnose/). No promises of recognition (conditional or not) will count.
* The countries have to recognize Palestine at the same time. If a country derecognises Palestine before the threshold of 4 countries has been reached it will not count.

title: When will the term of Israel's 25th Knesset end?
short_title: When will the term of Israel's 25th Knesset end?
description:
According to [the Atlantic](https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2025/07/netanyahu-coalition-falling-apart/683568/), Israel will probably have elections in early 2026:

> Given these proliferating threats to his position, Netanyahu has been doing what he does best: playing for time. The [summer recess](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/politics-and-diplomacy/article-795791) for Israel’s Parliament begins on July 27 and extends through the Jewish holidays, until late October. During that time, the Parliament cannot vote to dissolve itself, and so it would be hard for lawmakers to compel new elections. Netanyahu could reach a cease-fire in Gaza, for example, and the far-right would not be able to immediately bring down the coalition. The prime minister just has to run out the clock until the end of the month, and then he will have space either to get all of his partners back on his side—an unlikely prospect—or to make moves that upset his coalition but put him in a better position for the election that would be called upon the Parliament’s return.
> ‎
> Whenever that contest does happen—most likely around January—Netanyahu will face arguably the steepest political challenge of his career. Last election, his coalition received just [48.4 percent](https://votes25.bechirot.gov.il/) of the vote, attaining a parliamentary majority only because of a [technicality](https://www.cnn.com/2022/11/07/middleeast/netanyahu-election-threshhold-mime-intl/index.html) in Israel’s electoral system. That coalition has been losing in the polls since April 2023, and no amount of success against Hezbollah or Tehran has altered the trajectory. Thanks to his campaign in Iran, Netanyahu may be in his strongest position since the catastrophe of October 7. But after alienating so many of his allies and the [majority](https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2025/03/netanyahu-poll-numbers/682008/) of the Israeli people, that still might not be enough.

The next scheduled election is set for [October 27, 2026](https://www.timesofisrael.com/judge-sets-date-for-next-scheduled-elections-for-october-2026/).
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as either

* the date that Israel's 25th Knesset is formally dissolved

OR

* the date that Israel holds its next legislative election

whichever comes first.

title: Who will be the 2028 Democratic nominee for President of the United States?
short_title: Who will be the 2028 Democratic nominee for President of the United States?
description:
[Presidential elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2028_United_States_presidential_election?useskin=vector) are scheduled to be held in the United States on November 7, 2028, to elect a president and vice president for a term of four years. After winning a non-consecutive second term in the [2024 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election?useskin=vector), incumbent Republican Donald J. Trump, who was the nominee of the Republican Party in three consecutive elections, is prohibited by the [22nd Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-second_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution?useskin=vector) from being elected to a third term as president.

Incumbent President Joe Biden won the [2024 Democratic Party presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries), but subsequently [withdrew his candidacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withdrawal_of_Joe_Biden_from_the_2024_United_States_presidential_election) in July 2024, prior to the formal selection of the Democratic Party nominee. The withdrawal followed a June 27, 2024, debate with Donald Trump which raised questions about Biden's age and ability to serve a second term. Vice President [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris) received the Democratic Party's presidential nomination.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** for the person who is selected by the Democratic Party as the Democratic nominee for President of the United States for the [2028 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2028_United_States_presidential_election). If someone other than a named individual is selected this question will resolve as **Other**.

title: Will a federal law, regulation, or executive order mandating safety checks for AI models be enacted, issued, or adopted in the United States before January 20, 2029?
short_title: AI safety checks mandated before Jan 20, 2029?
description:
As artificial intelligence becomes more powerful, governments have started ramping up regulation to mitigate its negative effects. On August 1, 2024, EU's [Artificial Intelligence Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_Intelligence_Act) came into force, establishing a common regulatory and legal framework for AI within the EU. Similarly, in 2022, the White House released its "[AI Bill of Rights](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/ai-bill-of-rights)". In 2023, the Biden administration [secured voluntary AI safety commitments](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2023/07/21/fact-sheet-biden-harris-administration-secures-voluntary-commitments-from-leading-artificial-intelligence-companies-to-manage-the-risks-posed-by-ai/) from Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Inflection, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI, which were [later joined](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2023/09/12/fact-sheet-biden-harris-administration-secures-voluntary-commitments-from-eight-additional-artificial-intelligence-companies-to-manage-the-risks-posed-by-ai/) by Adobe, Cohere, IBM, Nvidia, Palantir, Salesforce, Scale AI, and Stability AI. According to [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulation_of_AI_in_the_United_States)

> The companies committed to ensure AI products undergo both internal and external security testing before public release; to share information on the management of AI risks with the industry, governments, civil society, and academia; to prioritize cybersecurity and protect proprietary AI system components; to develop mechanisms to inform users when content is AI-generated, such as watermarking; to publicly report on their AI systems' capabilities, limitations, and areas of use; to prioritize research on societal risks posed by AI, including bias, discrimination, and privacy concerns; and to develop AI systems to address societal challenges, ranging from cancer prevention to climate change mitigation.

Later in 2023, Biden signed [Executive Order 14110](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2023/10/30/fact-sheet-president-biden-issues-executive-order-on-safe-secure-and-trustworthy-artificial-intelligence/) (Executive Order on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence), defining the administration’s policy goals regarding AI and directing executive agencies to pursue them. According to the fact sheet, the Executive Order would

> *
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 21, 2029, a federal bill is signed into law, an executive order is issued, or a federal regulation is officially adopted in the United States that legally mandates that AI companies do at least one of the following:

* they conduct third-party safety evaluations of their frontier models
* they conduct internal safety evaluations of their frontier models and share their data or results with either the US government or third parties.
fine_print:
* This question is purposefully not defining "frontier models". Any such defintion by the bill, EO, or regulation would suffice to resolve this question, even if it is for a slightly different model class (e.g., "dangerous models"), as long as it is intended to cover all models from a capability level and above. This includes simple compute thresholds, benchmark results, or leaving the decision of what is considered a frontier model to the AI companies or the evaluators.
* The date the bill, EO, or regulation comes into effect is immaterial for the purposes of this question. It will resolve solely based on the date the bill is signed into law, the EO is issued, or the regulation is officially adopted.
* An Executive Order is any presidential document with an Executive Order number, published in the [Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/presidential-documents/executive-orders). Orders that do not have such a number will not count for this question. (See, e.g., US Library of Congress [discussion](https://guides.loc.gov/executive-orders/order-proclamation-memorandum) of EOs compared with other presidential directives.)

title: Will the US dollar continuously remain >50% of global foreign currency exchange reserves through Q3 2028?
short_title: USD world's reserve currency through Q3 2028
description:
According to [Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/r/reservecurrency.asp):

> A reserve currency is a large quantity of currency maintained by [central banks](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/centralbank.asp) and other major financial institutions to prepare for investments, transactions, and international debt obligations, or to influence their domestic exchange rate. A large percentage of commodities, such as gold and oil, are priced in the reserve currency, causing other countries to hold this currency to pay for these goods.

The Bretton Woods Agreement, [signed](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/brettonwoodsagreement.asp) by 44 countries during the waning days of World War II and fully implemented by 1958, established the US dollar as the global reserve currency, backed by gold. In 1971, the gold backing was removed, creating a freer floating exchange system, but with the US dollar largely maintaining its dominance through present day, with the dollar having maintained its dominance through the rest of the 20th Century. Since then, the dollar has slowly declined: 

![](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/Fyq73TxaEAgWqGF?format=jpg\&name=small) 

In measuring foreign currency reserves, there are 149 participating monetary authorities reporting to the IMF, making up, at the time of this question, 93% of total global foreign exchange reserves, which comprise the Allocated Reserves denominator of this question. resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as **Yes** if the US dollar is greater than 50% of global allocated foreign exchange reserves reported at the International Monetary Fund's Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserve (IMF COFER) [data page](https://data.imf.org/?sk=e6a5f467-c14b-4aa8-9f6d-5a09ec4e62a4) for each quarter after 2024 through and including the 3rd quarter of 2028.

If there is at least one quarter in which the US dollar is equal to or less than 50% of global allocated foreign exchange reserves, then this question resolves as **No**.

fine_print: If the IMF ceases publishing official figures on COFER, Metaculus may use an alternate resolution source provided the methodology is substantially similar. If none can be found, the question will be **annulled**.

title: Will a court change the winner of a 2026 election for U.S. House, Senate, or a top statewide office?
short_title: Will court change winner of '26 election for House, Senate or statewide office?
description: Legal challenges to election results, while rare, have occurred in past U.S. elections. Courts have intervened in cases involving [<u>ballot tampering</u>](https://ballotpedia.org/North_Carolina%27s_9th_Congressional_District_election,_2018), [<u>recounts and vote-counting procedures</u>](https://mn.electionarchives.lib.umn.edu/election/2320081099911600/), and [<u>allegations of fraud o</u>](https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/20/politics/paterson-new-jersey-city-council-voter-fraud/index.html)[<u>r election law violations</u>](https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/20/politics/paterson-new-jersey-city-council-voter-fraud/index.html). President Donald Trump and allies have made unproven claims of election fraud influencing the outcome of the 2020 presidential election and various state-level midterm elections. The recent rise in national disputes over the results of federal elections raise the possibility of court intervention in the 2026 midterms, particularly in closely divided states or congressional districts.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 1, 2028, a federal or state court issues a ruling that results in a change of the recognized winner according to the appropriate state election authorities of a 2026 election for one of the following offices:

* U.S. House of Representatives
* U.S. Senate
* Top statewide elected offices

If the state election authority does not officially determine a winner, the winner will be determined based on reporting by the Associated Press or another [credible source](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

If no election in one of the offices listed above has been overturned by a court before January 1, 2028, this question resolves as **No**.
fine_print:
* For the purposes of this question, a top statewide elected office is any of the following: governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, secretary of state, and state supreme court judges.
* The ruling must overturn the results such that the candidate initially reported as the winner according to the appropriate state election authorities is not the final winner and either another candidate is the winner or a new election must be held.
* The decision to hold a new election will be considered a change to the outcome regardless of who ultimately wins the new election.
* A recount called by the court will only suffice to resolve this question if it ends up changing the outcome of the election.
* If a decision is later overturned on appeal, it will still count.

title: Will the House of Representatives seat a legislator who was not certified as the winner of their election before July 1, 2027?
short_title: Will the House seat a legislator who was not certified winner before July 2027?
description: In recent years, President Donald Trump has [<u>asserted</u>](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/timeline-donald-trumps-election-denial-claims-republican-politicians/story?id=89168408) the existence of rampant election fraud, but has provided [<u>little to no evidence</u>](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/widespread-election-fraud-claims-by-republicans-dont-match-the-evidence/) to back up these assertions. Following his election loss in 2020, Trump [<u>pressured numerous state officials</u>](https://www.lawfaremedia.org/article/point-4-evidence-trump-tried-convince-state-lawmakers-and-election-officials-alter-election-results) to challenge certified results on the basis of fraud and corruption. If a Trump-aligned majority controls the House, they could theoretically [<u>use</u>](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/RL33780) Article I, Section 5 of the Constitution to refuse to seat certified members or seat their own choices under disputed election claims.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, at any time before July 1, 2027, the House of Representatives seats an individual as a member who was not certified as the winner of their election by the [<u>relevant state authorities</u>](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1d-V0OQGaN7TF289Qy4L8ot1kaZBFLD8BExHNhvQituw/edit?gid=420665400#gid=420665400). 

It will resolve as **No** if no such individual is seated by that time.
fine_print:
For the purposes of this question, the certified winner is the individual who has received an official certificate of election from the appropriate state authority. An individual is considered seated when they have taken the oath of office and are recognized as a member of the House of Representatives. This question pertains only to individuals elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.

We will rely on [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) for the resolution of this question.

title: Will the United States recognize Taiwan before January 20, 2029?
short_title: Will the US recognize Taiwan before January 20, 2029?
description:
On January 20, 2025, Donald J. Trump was inaugurated to a second term as US president. Within the first month of him taking office, the US State Department [updated](https://thediplomat.com/2025/02/did-the-us-just-change-its-taiwan-policy/) the language on its official page on Taiwan, dropping the sentence, "we do not support Taiwan independence." Additionally, members of the House of Representatives have [introduced a resolution](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2025/02/08/2003831541) calling for formal diplomatic recognition of Taiwan, which has gotten support from 22 Republican members of Congress.

According to the [US State Department](https://www.state.gov/countries-areas/taiwan/) at the current iteration of its Taiwan page:

> As a leading democracy and a technological powerhouse, Taiwan is a key U.S. partner in the Indo-Pacific. Though the United States does not have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, we have a robust unofficial relationship.

Under US law, only the US President has the power to recognize foreign states and governments. (See, e.g., [*Is the President's Recognition Power Exclusive*?](https://www.templelawreview.org/article/is-the-presidents-recognition-power-exclusive/) Volume 86, No. 1, Fall 2013 by Robert J. Reinstein.) When the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek moved to Taiwan in 1949, the US Embassy [moved to](https://history.state.gov/countries/china) Taipei, with the US recognizing the government of Taipei as the government of all of China, including the island of Taiwan and the mainland. This state of affairs remained until 1979, when President Jimmy Carter established diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, relocating the US embassy to Beijing, and terminated diplomatic relations with Taiwan.  

Today the US maintains unofficial relations through the [American Institute in Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Institute_in_Taiwan), which although it has certain functions that overlap with an embassy such as passport services, is not an official embassy and does not have an ambassador. 

As of the time of this question, only [12 countries](https://en.mofa.gov.tw/AlliesIndex.aspx?n=1294\&sms=1007) have diplomatic relations with Taiwan: Marshall Islands, Palau, Tuvalu, Eswatini, Holy See (Vatican City), Belize, Guatemala, Haiti, Paraguay, St. Kitts & Nevis, St. Lucia, and St. Vincent & the Grenadines.

title: Will a US federal court hold any part of the executive branch in contempt for not obeying a Supreme Court ruling, before January 20, 2029?
short_title: Executive branch in contempt for not obeying the Supreme Court, by Jan 20, 2029?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 20, 2029, any federal court or the Supreme Court of the United States formally holds any agency or official of the executive branch in contempt (civil or criminal) for either:

* direct non-compliance with a Supreme Court order, judgment, or mandate OR
* non-compliance with a federal court order that implements a Supreme Court mandate. For this to count, the contempt order has to explicitly cite that Supreme Court mandate.
fine_print:
* This question will resolve as **Yes** even if the contempt ruling is later reversed.
* Federal courts [consist of](https://www.justice.gov/usao/justice-101/federal-courts) federal district courts, circuit courts, and the Supreme Court.

title: Will the Trump administration announce a suspension of habeas corpus before January 20, 2029?
description: In May 2025, Stephen Miller, a senior advisor in the Trump administration, stated that the administration was “actively looking at” suspending the writ of habeas corpus to facilitate deportations, citing the constitutional provision allowing suspension [<u>“in time of invasion”</u>](https://time.com/7284743/what-is-habeas-corpus-under-threat-suspension-trump-administration/). This consideration arises amidst the administration’s invocation of the 1798 Alien Enemies Act to expedite the deportation of individuals, particularly targeting members of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua. The use of this wartime law has led to legal challenges and scrutiny over due process rights. The Supreme Court blocked the administration's attempt to use the AEA for deportation, emphasizing the need for adequate notice and [<u>the opportunity to challenge such actions under habeas corpus rights.</u>](https://time.com/7286140/supreme-court-immigration-aliens-act/)
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 20, 2029, the executive branch announces it is suspending the writ of habeas corpus in any part of the United States.

Resolution will be based on an official proclamation, executive order, Department of Justice memorandum, or other formal government action explicitly suspending the writ of habeas corpus that is intended to have the force of law according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
fine_print:
* The writ of habeas corpus refers to the constitutional right of individuals to challenge the legality of their detention before a court.
* Failures to grant habeas corpus to specific individuals or opposition to legal actions invoking habeas corpus in specific court cases will not suffice. There must be a general and formal suspension of the right.
* Suspension of habeas corpus is not necessarily universal — for example, it may apply only to a specific group (e.g., non-citizens), a particular region (e.g., border areas), or under defined conditions (e.g., national security emergencies). Any such announced suspension would still result in a **Yes** resolution.
* This question resolves based on an executive branch announcement of a suspension of habeas corpus that is intended to have the force of law. Therefore, its actual implementation, including such scenarios as being enjoined by courts, is immaterial for resolution.

title: Will the US establish a government program rewarding information leading to deportations before January 3, 2027?
short_title: Will a government program reward deportation tips before 2027?
description:
Throughout US history, there have been various forms of civilian tip lines and enforcement incentives related to immigration, but none yet offering paid rewards. Currently, the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tip line allows civilians to report suspected immigration violations, but it does not offer monetary incentives. Given the ongoing debates about immigration policy and border enforcement, there is a possibility that certain states or the federal government could introduce a monetary reward system to encourage civilian participation in deportation efforts.

*This forecast question was created by Bright Line Watch, a nonpartisan watchdog group. Forecast on their other questions* [*here*](https://www.metaculus.com/c/brightlinewatch/)*.*
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 3, 2027, a United States federal or state government formally establishes a program that provides monetary rewards to civilians for providing information leading to the deportation of individuals from the US.

For this question to resolve as Yes:

* The program must be officially established by a federal executive branch department (e.g., DHS, ICE, DOJ), a state executive branch agency, or a federal or state legislature through enacted legislation.
* The program must offer monetary compensation or financial incentives in exchange for providing information that contributes to the deportation of undocumented immigrants or individuals otherwise subject to removal proceedings.
* The program must become active before January 1, 2027.

This question will not resolve as Yes if:

* There is no monetary reward involved (e.g., a general tip line or anonymous reporting system without financial compensation).
* The program is proposed or debated but not officially established and implemented before the deadline.
* The program is created only by a private organization rather than a government entity.
* The monetary rewards are only offered to law enforcement officers or government employees, rather than civilians.

title: Will the US Dollar Index (DXY) drop below an average of 88 for any 90-day period before the 2029 presidential inauguration?
short_title: Will DXY’s 90-day average fall below 88 before Jan 20, 2029?
description:
The [US Dollar Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Dollar_Index) ticker symbol DXY and nicknamed the Dixie, is a weighted geometric mean of the US dollar (USD) compared with the following six currencies according to the Intercontinental Exchange ([pdf](https://www.ice.com/publicdocs/ICE_USDX_Brochure.pdf)) which maintains the index: 

* Euro 57.6%
* Japanese Yen 13.6%
* British Pound 11.9%
* Canadian Dollar 9.1%
* Swedish Krona 4.2%
* Swiss Franc 3.6%

The index began in 1973 and included a basket of European currencies that got consolidated into the Euro in 1999. The DXY's starting value in 1973 was 100, and subsequent changes in its value reflect its changes relative to that baseline. [According to Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/u/usdx.asp):

> An index value of 120 suggests that the U.S. dollar has appreciated 20% versus the basket of currencies over a particular time period. Simply put, if the USDX goes up, that means the U.S. dollar is getting stronger in value compared to the other currencies.

> Similarly, an index value of 80, indicating a fall of 20 from its initial value, implies a 20% depreciation in strength relative to the other currencies. The appreciation and depreciation results are a factor of the time period in question.

Over history, the DXY has fluctuated as follows, ranging from an all-time high of almost 165 in 1984 and an all time low of nearly 70 in 2007:

![](https://cdn.metaculus.com/user_uploaded/USDX_Blue-d93b4f708867472dba7a05f3b3f2fa0b.webp)

In April 2025, in the days following President Donald Trump's [Rose Garden announcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberation_Day_tariffs) of potential high tariffs and trade wars, the USD [fell](https://www.morningstar.com/markets/dollar-hits-3-year-low-against-euro-tariff-turmoil) against other major currencies, hitting a 10-year low against the Swiss franc and a 3-year low against the Euro. This fall was a surprise to many observers, with the tariffs [having been expected](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/04/06/trumps-tariffs-were-expected-to-boost-the-dollar-but-theyre-not.html) to boost the dollar. 

According to an analysis by [BNP Parabas](https://economic-research.bnpparibas.com/html/en-US/Could-Trump-drive-down-dollar-1/21/2025,51217): 

> Donald Trump’s position on the greenback is somewhat ambivalent and contradictory, straddled between maintaining its dominance and wanting to see it depreciate to boost the competitiveness of US exports. The
resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if at any point after the launch of this question and before January 20, 2029, the value of the US Dollar Index (DXY) averaged over any 90-day period is is less than 88.00, according to  [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/DX-Y.NYB/history/).
fine_print:
The 90-day period refers to calendar days rather than trading days and will be the arithmetic mean of the daily Close prices for DXY. For example, at the time of this question, the 90-day period January 25, 2025 through April 25, 2025 encompassed 63 trading days presented by Yahoo Finance and had an average daily Close value of 104.51.

Should the resolution source be at a different location, fail to exist at the time of resolution, or have clearly erroneous data, Metaculus may choose another appropriate resolution source.

The question may, at Metaculus' discretion, resolve as **No** before January 20, 2029 if it becomes mathematically impossible for the 90-day average through January 20, 2029 to be less than 88.00.

title: Will the size of the US Supreme Court increase before 2029?
short_title: Will the size of the US Supreme Court increase during Trump's second term?
resolution_criteria: If before January 1, 2029, [28 U.S. Code § 1](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/1) is amended to specify that the Supreme Court of the United States shall consist of greater than a total of 9 justices, then this question resolves as **Yes**. Otherwise it resolves as **No**.
fine_print:
Any change in the law must take effect on or before 1 Jan 2029; a law that goes into effect after this will not be sufficient, even if it has been enacted earlier.

This question will not consider the number of judges serving. Seats being vacant for any reason (including never being filled) will have no impact on this question.

This question resolves based on law that has been enacted: that is, passed by both Houses of Congress and received presidential signature, or via veto override.

This question will resolve based upon the time in Washington, D.C., which is the Eastern Time Zone of the US.

title: What percent of US GDP will come from manufacturing in the first half of 2028?
short_title: What percent of US GDP will come from manufacturing in the first half of 2028?
description:
One of the most fundamental patterns in economic development is the progression from agriculture and resource extraction to industry to services. In this [three-stage model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-sector_model), countries typically begin relying on primary activities, such as agriculture, mining, forestry, and fishing, then transition toward manufacturing and industrial production as productivity gains free up labor. In the final stage, mature economies pivot toward services. In the original model by Fisher, Clark, and Fourastié, these services were thought of as the transport, distribution and sale of goods, but later reconceptualisations of the model expanded the definition to include finance, healthcare, education, and entertainment.

This trend has become a particular concern for some US policymakers, with the GDP share of manufacturing dropping by more than a third from 1997 (16.1%) to 2021 (10.5%). At the same time the GDP share of manufacturing in the world dropped by less than 15 percent (from 19.0% to 16.5%).

<iframe src="https://data.worldbank.org/share/widget?indicators=NV.IND.MANF.ZS&locations=US-1W" width="600" height="450" frameborder="0" scrolling="no"></iframe>  
Declining manufacturing will likely have a negative impact on the US economy with [13 million workers](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/manufacturing-innovation-blog/manufacturing-america-contributing-our-economy-employment-and) employed in manufacturing jobs, and a large part of research and innovation being spearheaded by manufacturing companies. Indeed, some states would be [disproportionately affected](https://www.epi.org/publication/the-manufacturing-footprint-and-the-importance-of-u-s-manufacturing-jobs/#epi-toc-9) by manufacturing losses. Weak manufacturing would also lead to greater reliance on other countries and is thus often viewed as a [national security issue](https://www.cnas.org/publications/commentary/its-time-for-a-true-industrial-strategy-for-american-national-security); although [not everyone agrees](https://www.cato.org/publications/policy-analysis/manufactured-crisis-deindustrialization-free-markets-national-security#).

For these reasons, Trump [pledged](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/24/us/politics/trump-economic-policy.html) during his campaign that he would implement policies to increase the manufacturing capacity of the US. These included the early 2025 tariffs, but also other actions, such as the [removal of regulatory barriers](https://
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the average manufacturing share of GDP for Q1 and Q2, 2028, reported in the FRED series [Value Added by Industry: Manufacturing as a Percentage of GDP](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/VAPGDPMA) (VAPGDPMA).
fine_print: This question will resolve after both values have been published by FRED and when they are first accessed by Metaculus. Later revisions will not impact resolution.

title: Will the US government order the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) or NASDAQ to be closed before January 20, 2029?
short_title: Trump closes NYSE or NASDAQ before January 20, 2029?
description:
The [New York Stock Exchange](https://www.nyse.com/index) (NYSE) and the [National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations](https://www.nasdaq.com) (Nasdaq) are the two largest stock exchanges in the world by market capitalization, ranked 1st and 2nd respectively.

Both stock exchanges run year round, closing only on weekends and on recognized holidays such as Christmas Day and New Years day; or during National Days of Mourning, like when the late President Jimmy Carter passed away; or for extended periods of time in more exceptional circumstances such as:

* World Wars 1 and 2.
* Great Depression Banking Crisis.
* September 11 Attacks.

The historical precedent for the above closures were to stabilize the markets by preventing large sell-offs and to stem panic. They have typically been executed in coordination with the US government, rather than a Presidential order for example.

President Donald Trump, during both his first term and ongoing second term, has been a frequent commenter on the stock market and its governing institutions. Trump has [publicly called](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-04-23/powell-attempts-balancing-act-as-trump-tests-fed-s-autonomy) for current Chairman Jerome Powell to lower interest rates, something many observe as an infringement of the Federal Reserve's autonomy. Indeed, Trump has also had internal discussions on having [Powell removed](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/04/23/business/trump-jerome-powell/index.html), which would be an unprecedented decision with no clear legal basis and something his closest advisors strongly advised against<sup>1</sup>. Trump has also [attacked](https://x.com/TrumpDailyPosts/status/1834712936952349040) the SEC and the Nasdaq after halting trading of [Trump Media & Technology Group Corp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_Media_%26_Technology_Group) (\$DJT), a company majority-owned by Trump, due to volatility - a very normal procedure for any stock:

> Why is NASDAQ halting the sale of DJT? What right do they have to do this? \[...] Are they taking orders from the SEC, which, for political reasons, delayed us for an inordinate amount of time, therefore hurting the stock very badly? I am going to hold NASDAQ, and maybe the SEC, liable for doing what they are doing.

Moreover, Trump has often [linked](https://x.com/TrumpDailyPosts/status/1752035267274518696) stock market performance to government performance and success, but, in light of his tariff campaign, the st
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 20, 2029, the US government orders the [New York Stock Exchange](https://www.nyse.com/index) (NYSE) or the [National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations](https://www.nasdaq.com) (Nasdaq) stock markets to be closed for one or more entire regularly-scheduled trading days.
fine_print:
Note that stock market closures ordered for the following reasons will **not** be sufficient to resolve the question to **Yes**:

* National Days of Mourning.
* National Holidays.
* Natural Disasters (e.g., hurricanes, volcanic eruptions etc.)

Closures due to other reasons would be sufficient.

Requests or pressure to close made by the government but without a formal order (for example, see the [1914 closure of the NYSE](https://elischolar.library.yale.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1346\&context=journal-of-financial-crises)) do **not** count.

Whether an order is followed and subsequent challenges to the legality of such an order are immaterial, the question immediately will resolve when a qualifying order is made.

title: Who will win the 2026 California gubernatorial election?
short_title: Who will win the 2026 California gubernatorial election?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the winner of the 2026 California gubernatorial election.
fine_print:
If a candidate other than one of the listed candidates wins the election, this question will resolve as **Other**.

This question will resolve based upon the final general election winner. In the event of a dispute, this question will resolve based upon the determination of the State of California or may be **annulled**.

title: Which party will win the 2026 Maine gubernatorial election?
short_title: Which party will win the 2026 Maine gubernatorial election?
description: The [2026 Maine gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Maine_gubernatorial_election) will elect the successor to Democratic Governor [Janet Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Mills), who is term-limited and cannot seek a third consecutive term. The primary is scheduled for June 9, 2026, and the general election for November 3, 2026. Gubernatorial elections in Maine are decided by plurality. The Democratic and Republican primaries are both contested, while several independent candidates are also seeking ballot access, including state senator [Rick Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Bennett_\(Maine_politician\)).
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve based on the party or ballot affiliation of the candidate elected governor of Maine in the 2026 general election, after any run off rounds or recounts, according to the officially announced election results.

This question will resolve as **Other** if the elected governor does not belong to the Democratic or Republican party.

title: Which party will win the 2026 Alaska gubernatorial election?
short_title: Which party will win the 2026 Alaska gubernatorial election?
description: The 2026 Alaska gubernatorial election will elect Alaska's next governor and lieutenant governor. Incumbent Republican Governor [Mike Dunleavy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Dunleavy_\(politician\)) is term-limited and cannot seek a third consecutive term. Alaska uses a nonpartisan blanket primary, in which all candidates appear on the same primary ballot and the top four advance to the general election, which is conducted using [ranked-choice voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranked_voting). The primary is scheduled for August 18, 2026, and the general election for November 3, 2026. The field includes several Republican and Democratic candidates, with early polling [showing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Alaska_gubernatorial_election#Polling) a fragmented race and a large share of undecided voters.
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve based on the party or ballot affiliation of the candidate elected governor of Alaska in the 2026 general election, after any run off rounds or recounts, according to the officially announced election results.

This question will resolve as **Other** if the elected governor does not belong to the Democratic or Republican party.

title: What will be the Republican advantage (or disadvantage) vs Democrats in the House of Representatives after the 2026 elections?
short_title: GOP House advantage after 2026 midterms?
description:
Every 2 years, the United States elects all 435 members of the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives), as well as one-third of the 100 members of the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate). As of October 2025, Republicans hold a slim majority of 219 seats in the House, one of 53 seats in the Senate, and the Presidency. Recent decades have been [highly competitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate#/media/File:Combined--Control_of_the_U.S._House_of_Representatives_-_Control_of_the_U.S._Senate.png). In the [last 10 midterm elections](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/data/seats-congress-gainedlost-the-presidents-party-mid-term-elections), the party opposing the President gained a median of 11 seats in the House, and gained at least one seat in 8 out of 10 years.

[The election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections) is currently scheduled for November 3, 2026.
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the number of seats won by Republicans minus the number of seats won by Democrats in the US House of Representantives at the 2026 midterm elections.
fine_print:
* Independent or third-party candidates who are known to caucus with one party will be included in the count for the relevant party.
* If the Democrats win more seats than the Republicans, this question will resolve as a negative number.
* This number will be determined by whomever won their elections, following any runoff elections or recounts, according to credible sources. It will not necessarily reflect the House Membership or party control at any particular time (e.g., if members retire or are appointed during the counting and resolution of votes).

title: Which party will control the US Congress following the 2026 midterm elections?
short_title: US Congress Control After 2026 Midterms
description:
From [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_elections):

> The **2026 United States elections** are scheduled to be held, in large part, on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. In this [U.S. midterm election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._midterm_election "U.S. midterm election"), which will occur during [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_\(United_States\) "Republican Party (United States)") President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s non-consecutive second term, all 435 seats in the [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives "U.S. House of Representatives") and 33 of the 100 seats in the [U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate "U.S. Senate") will be contested to determine the [120th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/120th_United_States_Congress "120th United States Congress"). Thirty-nine state and territorial [U.S. gubernatorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._gubernatorial "U.S. gubernatorial") elections, as well as numerous state and local elections, will also be contested.
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as the configuration of party control that results from the 2026 US congressional elections (following runoffs or recounts, as applicable), subject to the following criteria:

* If one party holds more than 50% of seats in a chamber of Congress, that party will be considered to control that chamber.
* For the Senate, if seats are tied exactly 50-50 between two parties, the Senate will be considered controlled by the party of the President of the United States.
* If, following the swearing-in of new congresspeople at the beginning of the 2027 session, control of a chamber of Congress remains ambiguous, Metaculus will delay the resolution of this question until the election of the leader of that chamber (Speaker of the House or Senate Majority Leader), following which, the chamber shall be considered to be controlled by the party of the Speaker or Majority Leader.  For the purposes of this question, an Independent or third party House Speaker or Majority Leader will be considered to belong to the party with which they caucus.
* If, following the election of leadership of both chambers of Congress, control of either or both chambers remains unclear, Metaculus may rely on a consensus of credible sources or may resolve this question **Ambiguous**.
fine_print: * As used above, "seats" refers to those held by voting members of the US Congress.  Seats held by non-voting members, such as [non-voting representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-voting_members_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives) from the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, etc., will not be considered when assessing control of a chamber.

title: What will be the Republican advantage (or disadvantage) vs Democrats in the Senate after the 2026 elections?
short_title: GOP Senate advantage after 2026 midterms?
description:
Every 2 years, the United States elects all 435 members of the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives), as well as one-third of the 100 members of the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate). As of October 2025, Republicans hold a slim majority of 219 seats in the House, one of 53 seats in the Senate, and the Presidency. In the [last 10 midterm elections](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/data/seats-congress-gainedlost-the-presidents-party-mid-term-elections), the party opposing the President gained a median of 3.5 seats in the House, and gained at least one seat in 6 out of 10 years.

fine_print:
* Independent or third-party senators who are known to caucus with one party before January 4, 2027 will be included in the count for the relevant party. If they aren't known to caucus with any party by that date, they will not be included in the resolution of this question.
